strategy.summary: Reproduce SciPy numerical-accuracy regression for the Crystalball survival function (sf) at large x, by running SciPy’s stats test suite on the buggy revision ed184ffc1994 and verifying the dedicated ROOT-derived regression assertions in test_distributions.py fail there and pass after the PR #21358 fix.

build_commands:
# Create isolated environment
python -m venv venv && . venv/bin/activate
pip install -U pip setuptools wheel cython numpy pybind11

# Get SciPy source at buggy commit
git clone https://github.com/scipy/scipy.git
cd scipy
git checkout ed184ffc1994

# Build/install SciPy (editable recommended for iterative debugging)
pip install -e .[test]
pinned_because: NumPy/SciPy/ROOT have unbounded era constraints and no explicit pinned versions were provided in the evidence; choose stable, modern versions that support building SciPy with wheels/build-from-source for the target platform.

strategy.reproducing_test: Within scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py, class TestCrystalBall::test_sf (and optionally test_cdf/pdf as sanity) as added/changed by PR #21358. This test asserts crystalball.sf(x,beta,m) equals ROOT-computed reference rootref for several x including large positive x: (12.0,1.0,2.0),(9.0,4.0,1.25),(20,0.1,1.001).
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision ed184ffc1994, running the crystalball-focused pytest selection fails at least one assert_allclose inside TestCrystalBall.test_sf due to loss of precision for large x (x > -beta). On the fixed revision (merge result of scipy/scipy#21358), the same command passes because crystalball_gen._sf uses the improved branch logic computing the Gaussian-regime SF as a multiple of the normal SF.
strategy.numerical_probe: The relevant numerical regime is for large x where crystalball.sf should follow the Gaussian regime identity for x > -beta. The test probes this via ROOT reference values rootref at x=9.0, 12.0, 20 for parameters (beta,m) that satisfy x > -beta.

risks: This strategy assumes SciPy can be built in your environment; exact build dependencies (BLAS/LAPACK, Fortran compiler) are not specified in the evidence.

The evidence does not provide explicit platform/toolchain requirements; if the bug only triggers under a specific BLAS backend, CPU architecture (e.g., x86 vs ARM), or floating-point mode, the test failure might not reproduce elsewhere.

Because dependency era constraints are unbounded for NumPy/SciPy/ROOT in the evidence, version skew could change numerical behavior and might weaken/alter the failure; if the failure does not reproduce, adjust NumPy version within the same major release line and rerun only the crystalball tests.
The exact ‘fixed’ commit SHA is not provided; you must check out the PR’s post-fix revision (merge commit or commit after ed184ffc1994) to confirm the transition.

oracle.reference_source: ROOT-independent reference constants embedded in the PR-added TestCrystalBall.test_sf parametrize table (rootref).
oracle.why: The test uses assert_allclose(sf, rootref, rtol=1e-13) on the scalar/array outputs from stats.crystalball.sf; it fails when the relative error exceeds the rtol for the listed rootref values.

fails_on_buggy.description: Assertion seen in buggy revision: TestCrystalBall.test_sf does not satisfy assert_allclose(sf, rootref, rtol=1e-13) for one or more large-x cases, because the sf computed in crystalball_gen._sf loses precision in the x > -beta (Gaussian regime) branch.

passes_on_fixed.description: With the PR #21358 fix applied (improved _sf computation using the _norm_pdf_C*_norm_sf(x)/M rhs branch for x > -beta), the same assert_allclose checks pass for all rootref cases in TestCrystalBall.test_sf.
